utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Can we kindly have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour pleases, my name is Grant Niemann and I appear with my colleague Mr. Khan for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honours. I am Edina Residovic, appearing on behalf of Mr. Zejnil Delalic together with my colleague Eugene O'Sullivan, professor from Canada.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Good morning. I am Zeljko Olujic appearing on behalf of Mr. Zdravko Mucic together with my co-counsel Michael Greaves, attorney from the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honour. I am Salih Karabdic, attorney from Sarajevo, appearing on behalf of Mr. Hazim Delic, together with Mr. Thomas Moran, attorney from Houston Texas.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good morning. I am John Ackerman and along with Cynthia McMurrey we appear on behalf of Mr. Esad Landzo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Can we now have the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Perhaps before the witness comes in, your Honours, it is our intention after this witness to call a witness in relation to records, custodian of records from Sarajevo. If this witness is not completed by tomorrow morning I will make an application to interpose General Divjak on this witness because General Divjak has some commitments which he is unable to move commencing on Thursday morning first thing. So if your Honours please, I just wish to indicate that will be an application I will make should it become necessary. It may not become necessary. I do not expect the custodian of records will take that long, certainly not in chief anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was our understanding that Mr. Economides would be here on Tuesday and that was the only day he could appear; has that changed?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It has your Honour, Professor Economides is available on Thursday which gives us better time to accommodate General Divjak, so he will be available on Thursday. I am also able to announce to the Chamber that we have secured some articles written by Professor Economides which are being copied and will be made available to the Defence as soon as possible this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, does that satisfy you?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: (Nods).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Let us have the witness. (Witness enters court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Good morning, General. You are still under cross-examination. Please remind him he is still on his oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I am reminding you, sir, that you are still under oath. GENERAL ARIF PASALIC (continued) Cross-examination by MS. RESIDOVIC (continued)

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honours. Good morning, General. At the beginning of my cross-examination on Thursday I drew your attention to the problems of communication and I think we functioned very well, because you waited for the interpretation of my questions into English. Will you please bear that in mind today as well. Secondly, I should like to ask you, General, in the interest of expediency with respect to this part of the cross-examination, will you please answer my questions as concisely as possible, if possible with yes and no, when that is possible, of course. If brief explanation is necessary of course feel free to make them, but for any lengthier explanations we may come back to that at the end of the cross-examination. Also, for your benefit I should like to add that I noticed on Thursday that you wanted to ask some questions; according to the rules of this Tribunal it is the attorney who asks the questions and the witness who answers. We are not in a position to change those rules. I think we have now explained some additional procedural matters. Have I made myself clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have understood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, we broke off on Thursday when we were discussing the criminal charges which you or somebody on your behalf issued on 22nd December, 1992, against Zejnil Delalic and Zdravko Mucic. Do you remember that is where we interrupted our conversation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The witness' microphone is not switched on, or something is wrong. I should like to suggest that we discuss further the investigation that you instructed the commission to carry out when you became Corps Commander at the end of 1992, and when you heard about various irregularities in Konjic. You have already said quite a bit about that in answer to the question of the Prosecutor, as well as in answer to mine; but I should like to ask you for us to focus on a few matters still further. To that end, I would like to ask a representative of the Registry to show the General, once again, document D141, fully respecting the limitations indicated by the Prosecutor in connection with this document. General, we were discussing this document only to a limited extent. We will be speaking only about the names that appear or do not appear in this document, regarding the positions and responsibilities held by the names indicated in that document. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you this document on Wednesday or Thursday, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is criminal charges dated 22nd December, 1992, is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, can you tell the court whether it is true that these are the only charges which you or anybody else submitted on your behalf against Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I am concerned as Corps Commander, and my command, I think that these were the only criminal charges pressed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Though on Thursday, at my request, as well as at the request of my learned colleague the Prosecutor, you read the text, I should like to ask you to read very carefully the text of these charges, not to mention anything regarding the contents, just to read it for yourself, and to pay attention to the limited scope of the questions I am going to ask you, that is the names of the persons, their positions, and their responsibilities. (Pause).

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true, General, that in this document, the criminal charges, the following names appear: Zejnil Delalic and Zdravko Mucic, against whom the criminal charges have been brought, and in connection with which your commission elucidated certain irregularities, is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do not wish to mention any names; but will you please tell me, General, is it true that in this document not a single name is indicated of a member of Serbian ethnicity, of a person of Serbian ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what they are of ethnicity, but judging by their names and surnames I think not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also true, General, that you have indicated -- you have not indicated in this document anywhere the words "Serbian prisoner"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, those words are not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, to eliminate any possible misunderstanding or confusion, will you confirm the following: neither you nor your commission, since these were the only charges, ever pressed charges against Zejnil Delalic in connection with any criminal offences against prisoners of Serb ethnicity, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, do you recall that you said before this Trial Chamber, that at the end of 1992 there were reports in the media that you had allegedly claimed that Zejnil Delalic, at the end of November 1992, had fled to the Serb side, and, as reported in the press at the time, he fled by means of a Serb helicopter; is that not what you said in answer to a question by the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I said that there were various reports; among others, there was one to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, even though this was an article, and there were such articles, particularly in the Croatian press, you can assert before this Trial Chamber that you never said anything of the like and that that is either slander or propaganda?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not have said where Zejnil Delalic went until I received specific information about it. I do not know where the information came from that appeared in the press.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Though, as far as you remember, there were various media reporting on this, mostly the Croatian media. What they had in common was that Delalic and Mucic had fled over to the Serb side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot exactly remember which media carried such reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they said that they had fled to the Serb side, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly what they said. There were various assumptions and various reports in the press, either to the Serbian territory or Croatian territory. I had no opportunity to follow those reports in view of what was happening down there at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. To avoid spending too much time on media reports in wartime, but I would like us to go back to some more specific issues now. In answer to a question of the Prosecution you said that by pressing charges you did not wish to prejudge the outcome?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, General, that in our country criminal proceedings are conducted by courts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, General, that criminal proceedings are conducted upon the request of an authorised prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not very knowledgeable regarding legal procedure. I know that it was my duty to bring criminal charges for the persons that I felt this was warranted. What the further proceedings of the prosecution and the court are, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that in answer to a question put to you in this Trial Chamber you said that at the time when you came to Konjic there was no court or prosecutor's office which could prosecute such persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was ordered and given the suggestion that I should issue those charges and submit them to the district military prosecutor's office in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The district military prosecutor's office in Mostar, and the district military tribunal in Mostar were institutions that were operational at the time, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My orders were to submit them to the prosecution. Whether they were operational, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, even though perhaps you are no expert in legal matters, just as I am no expert in military matters, still there are some things that you know as a citizen. You must know that when proceedings are instituted against a person the upshot may be either the release, acquittal of that person, or his sentencing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Acquittal may be achieved if the prosecutor withdraws charges, or the court passes such a decision. But in any event, it is the court that decides to interrupt proceedings or acquit somebody of the charges?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should now like to ask the witness to be shown a document that the Prosecutor has a copy of; and could a copy be given to the Trial Chamber, and the Prosecution, so I may put some additional questions? Can you, please, tell me the number of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence document D82/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, will you please read this document carefully, and bear in mind the limitations that I referred to earlier on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, in the case of this document too we shall only be referring to the names appearing in it and the positions and responsibilities of the persons listed in that document. In order to identify the document, will you please tell me whether, in the top corner of the document, you find the name of the body that is the district military court in Mostar, the number of the document, K1/93, the place and date, that is Mostar, 21st February, 1994. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that in the signature you find the name, investigating magistrate, Drago Bevanda?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, General, that with this document the tribunal is terminating proceedings against Zejnil Delalic and Zdravko Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is a decision to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please can the document be returned to the Registry? General, the names Zejnil Delalic and Zdravko Mucic are names of persons that your commission investigated in connection with irregularities that you referred to in your interview in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should now like to ask you, General, to look at another document. The Prosecutor has a copy and I have sufficient copies for their Honours, the Prosecution and the Registry. Could the document be marked, please, and shown to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit D83/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please read this document too, bearing in mind the limitations that we have discussed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to identify the document, is it true that in the left corner of this document is the name of the body, military prosecutor's office, Mostar, number KT123/92, Mostar, 18th February 1994? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this document signed by the public prosecutor Mladen Jurisic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this document whereby the prosecutor is proposing the charges, do you find the names Zejnil Delalic and Zdravko Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this document their positions or responsibilities are not indicated, are they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they are not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those are the same persons that your commission investigated in connection with certain irregularities that you referred to in your interview in Jablanica, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can the document be returned to the Registry, please? General, are you aware that in our country persons may ask the appropriate court for information as to whether any criminal proceedings are being conducted against them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the security services in our country keep records of any punishment pronounced against any persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Counsel, I should like to show you some documents to examine. I have sufficient number of copies for you, the Trial Chamber and the Prosecution, so could the usher show the documents to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit D84/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I think we have not provided the English translation as well, so could those be given to the Trial Chamber as well, please? General, will you please look at the document dated 7th April, 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have looked at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this piece of paper you have two certificates, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The top certificate has an indication in the left-hand corner, the name of the body that issue it, Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, basic court in Konjic, the number of the document, the time and place when it was issued, Konjic, 7th April, 1994. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the bottom of this certificate, you see the stamp of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina of the basic court in Konjic, is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document was signed on behalf of the President of the court, by Sajin Aida -- at the bottom you see another certificate issued by the district military court in Mostar, department Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document too was issued in Konjic on 7th April, 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the bottom you see the stamp of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the district military tribunal in Mostar, department Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This certificate has also been signed by the head of the department, has it not? The signature is for, on behalf of the head of the department?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you have read both these certificates, is it true to say, General, that these courts indicated in the heading of the certificate confirmed that on 7th April, 1994 no criminal proceedings were conducted before these courts against Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you, please, General, now look at the document dated 4th April, 1995? This document has been copied in two ways, twice actually by mistake, so you can now have a look at whichever one is more legible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have looked at the documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, General, that in the top left corner of this certificate there is the name of the organ and that is the district military court in Mostar, Konjic department?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that there is also the number of the certificate, the place and the date of the issuance, Konjic, 4th April, 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that in the left -- in the right corner of this certificate there is the name of the organ, the basic court in Konjic, and the number under which this certificate has been registered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that below the certificate there are stamps of the district military tribunal in Mostar, Konjic department, and the stamp of the basic court in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that this certificate has been signed by the head of the department, Sulejman Bajric, and the President of the Basic Court, Halil Gagula?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that by this certificate these courts confirm that on 4th April, 1995 no criminal proceedings were conducted against Zejnil Delalic before those courts, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could these documents please be returned to the Registry. I would now like to ask you, General, to have a look at the following document. I have sufficient number of copies in Bosnian and English for the Trial Chamber, and I would like the original of the certificate to be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence document 85/1. Have you read the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, General, that this certificate was issued by the district military tribunal in Mostar, and the number and the date is the 16th May, 1996, indicated at the top left corner of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, General, that at the bottom of the certificate there is the stamp of the republic of Bosnian Herzegovina district military tribunal, Mostar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that this certificate was signed by the President of the tribunal, Asim Suta?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that the certificate confirms that Zejnil Delalic is not subject to any criminal proceedings and that he has not been entered in the criminal records of the court, of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, I would like this document to be returned to the Registry. I would like to show you another document, General. I have a sufficient number of copies for the Trial Chamber and for the Prosecution, and the Prosecutor is in possession of this document. I would like this document to be numbered.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is the Exhibit D86/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I raise a matter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you may.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, there has been a succession of these documents shown to the witness and in many respects this witness is not a terribly appropriate witness to be dealing with them. I have not objected, but I do question the relevance of it, in view of the basis on which the Prosecution at least has sought to tender the original exhibits which dealt with these proceedings. We have seen a -- I mean, I have raised no objection because I assumed counsel wanted to make it clear that proceedings did not go ahead. I have no problem with that. How much more are we to receive of these sorts of documents on what is ultimately an irrelevant issue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, have you any answers to that?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I showed the original of the document to the witness this time. We do not expect the witness to verify these documents at all, and as you can see I did not tender them as evidence. This is the last document in this series, and I have limited myself with regard to all these documents only to the name of Zejnil Delalic, which appears in these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually the observation is as to the relevance of them. If they are relevant to the question you are asking then there might be some point. What is your intention? What are you trying to show that they represent?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: They represent an answer to some of the questions, some of the issues raised by the Prosecutor when he discussed with this witness the commission and the interview shown before this Trial Chamber, since all of these documents contain the name of Zejnil Delalic, and it may have some relation to the evidence presented by the Prosecutor before this Trial Chamber. This is where we see the relevance of the documents we have shown here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Well, of course. It depends on the way you consider your own case. If all the earlier documents you are showing was that a person of that name and title -- that might be relevant, and you might have been able to show that this is an equation of that same name and title. It does not go further than that. I do not think they show anything more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, on Wednesday and Thursday we saw that in relation to the contents of the documents we have limited our examination to the -- only to the name of Zejnil Delalic and this witness has been shown a large number of documents and since this witness has confirmed that these issues were -- documents were issued by the bodies named on these documents. He can just confirm to us that these are the documents which are usually issued by such bodies at that time, and that these documents contain the name of Zejnil Delalic; and this is precisely what you suggested to us when we raised certain objections to some documents being shown to this witness while he was being questioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: As I said, I do not think one really minds but it is merely confirming what the Prosecution said.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, have you looked at this document; and of course, as I have already explained to you on Thursday, I do not want you to confirm the validity of any of these documents because you were not the person who issued them. Can you please tell me whether this document was issued by the Ministry of the Interior security services centre, Mostar, Konjic public security station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is what it says in the heading.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that this document was signed by the chief Amir Begic as indicated at the bottom of the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that this document mentions the name of Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And according to this document he does not have a criminal record of previous convictions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is what it says in the text.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like this document to be returned to the Registry. General, I would like to ask you now to go back to some other issues that you have discussed in part before this Trial Chamber. Is it true that you said that you had been to Konjic on several occasions and that you had discussed some issues with Rusmir Hadzihuseinovic, the chairman of the municipality, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that period you also talked to Jasmin Guska, who was the acting chief of the Ministry of the Interior in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I only met him once and it was a very brief meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what you said when the Prosecutor asked you that, but I would like you to be more specific and to agree with me, if possible; is it true that MUP, Ministry of the Interior, had its own chain of command and that at that time it did not accept to be placed under the overall command of the military armed forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not true that they did not place itself under the command of the armed forces. MUP, Ministry of the Interior, is a constituent part of the armed forces. The securities services centre in Mostar and the public security station in Konjic was part of that -- according to the Armed Forces Act of Bosnian Herzegovina was a part of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am referring to that period in time, that is the beginning and mid 1992, when that Act was not in force at the time. Is it true that the Ministry of the Interior had its own chain of command and it was subordinated to the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It probably had its own chain of command, but I cannot tell you anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you passed through Konjic, you probably talked to Dinko Zebic, the HVO commander, and Ivica Azinovic, his deputy, and President of the HVO, which was equivalent to the War Presidency in Konjic. Did you talk to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember having talked to them. I only visited the municipal headquarters in Konjic once with Jasmin Jaganjac. We did not find anyone there except for some soldiers who were on guard duty. I did not talk to the representatives of the HVO in Konjic at all in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you can confirm that you know the commanders of the Territorial Defence headquarters, Mirsad Catic and Esad Ramic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I met them during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can confirm, surely, that Zejnil Delalic was not a commander of the municipal headquarters of the Territorial Defence in Konjic, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know whether he was a commander or not. I know that Esad Ramic was a commander and later on it was Mirsad Catic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like now to ask you to look at a document. I have a sufficient number of copies -- number of copies both in Bosnian and in English. The Prosecution is in possession of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D87/1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have read the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, you know Commander Mustafa Polutak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know that in 1996 he was the Commander of the 4th Corps of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, General, that this document was issued by the command of the 4th Corps, headquartered in Jablanica on 22nd May, 1992, as it is indicated in the top left corner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that at the bottom of this document there is a stamp of the 4th Corps command and the signature of the Commander, Mustafa Polutak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that in this document the name of Zejnil Delalic is mentioned and that on the basis of the existing documents it is indicated that he has not been named as the Commander of the TO in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like the document now to be returned to the Registry. Your Honours, bearing in mind the time and the fact that I am about to start a new line of questioning, maybe it would be advisable to have a break now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You still have 20 minutes to continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. General, the Prosecutor showed you a document yesterday, it was a document by General Blaskic regarding the situation in central Bosnia. It is the Prosecution Exhibit number 78, and I would like you to have a look at it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Excuse me, your Honour, it does not appear to be exhibit 78.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: 188. Well, it seems that there is a problem with the interpretation, but I think that the Registry understands me well and that they have presented the witness with the right document. This document, according to what is stated in the document, was signed by Colonel Tihomir Blaskic, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This report also has to do for the period between 5th and 10th August 1992, as indicated under point 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have spoken about that, and will you please confirm that it was precisely in this period of time that heavy fighting was going on in order to lift the blockade of Sarajevo in the area of Igman, Pazaric and Ormanja -- that is in the area belonging to the area of responsibility of Zejnil Delalic as Commander of Tactical Group 1, is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, precisely in that period in August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also true, General, that this area of responsibility physically and territorially, if I may say so, bordered on the area of responsibility of Kiseljak, which was under the command of General Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The areas of responsibility of the operative zone, operative groups of the HVO and our own, that is of the BiH army and the Tactical Groups, overlapped, and this also applied to this area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also on Thursday you referred to certain disputes and obstructions put up at the time by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are surely aware that at that time in the area of Igman and Trnovo, the Commander of Tactical Group 2 was Mirsad Catic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that he was the commander, but I know that there were struggles to lift the blockade of Sarajevo. Who was in charge of the Tactical Group, this can surely be checked in documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that at the heat of those battles our units were obstructed from passing from Visoko and Fojnica towards the battle front within the area of responsibility of Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Regarding such obstructions of the movement of BiH army units, I heard about them, but I am not familiar with the details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also hear that between the 4th and the 8th August, in Kiseljak, the Commander of the TO headquarters, Sead Sinanbasic, members of the staff, were arrested and the public security station and the TO headquarters were seized?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about those arrests, but I am not familiar with the details concerning those arrested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, General, that all those activities and obstructive efforts were a hindrance and obstructed the efforts of our fighters to lift the blockade of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Semsudin Hasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that he was Chief of Staff of the 1st Mostar Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was for a time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please look at the next document, of which we have sufficient copies in English and Bosnian, so could they be identified and marked and shown to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is D88/1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before I ask you any questions about this document, I want to ask you something which may be quite clear, but as a layman not quite. Is it true, General, that a superior military officer addressing a subordinate officer or any other subordinate uses orders, requests and commands?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Will you please repeat that question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A commander or a senior officer in the military, when addressing any subordinate, an officer, a senior officer or a soldier, does he do so by issuing orders or commands?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, generally speaking, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, at the top of this document you see the heading, "the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina army of Bosnia-Herzegovina 1st Mostar Brigade", is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the Brigade that you headed from the middle of July, when it was formed, until you became Corps Commander, is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you have already indicated, at the time your Chief of Staff was Semsudin Hasic, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In answer to a question from the Prosecution on Thursday -- Wednesday and Thursday, you said that when passing through Konjic you most frequently discussed with persons you met the needs regarding defence and any possible exchange of those resources or needs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document, which was addressed by the 1st Mostar Brigade to Mr. Zejnil Delalic in person, is it one of those documents whereby you are asking a certain amount of ammunition to be provided to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did ask for ammunition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you, General, know Major Sefkija Kevric, assistant for logistics of the municipal TO staff in Konjic at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I met him later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, General, that the signature of this hand-written text, Delalic, Zejnil, is asking this person to meet, asking Sefkija Kevric to meet your requirement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it follow from the contents of this request, General, that Zejnil Delalic, in this period too, that is 10th November 1992, was in a certain sense engaged with logistical issues?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. General, I apologise, I seem to be losing my tie. In the course of your examination-in-chief, the Prosecutor showed you a number of documents that were hand-written. Is it true, General, that you do not know who, when or on what occasion compiled and wrote those documents? There were several documents that were hand-written by somebody?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know which documents you are referring to you. There were such documents that were shown to me that the signature is not legible, nor the stamp, nor is it certified.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when those documents were shown to you, you did not in any sense identify or authenticate those documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I object to the question and that broad a way of putting it. I have no objection to a question, "you did not authenticate the writing"; certainly I did not ask this witness to identify the writing. I asked certain questions about the documents. I object to the question on the basis of its width. I do not object to a question about whether or not he was asked or whether he can authenticate. It was never suggested he could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Perhaps you could ask whether he is acquainted with this handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I did not ask that. She is certainly entitled to ask it. I would not object to that, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions regarding those documents. I just wanted to make it clear precisely what my learned colleague the Prosecutor has just said. I accept the objection this time. General, the Prosecutor showed you a document marked D189, so could it be shown to the General once again, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is Prosecution document 189.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In connection with the questions put to you regarding this document by the Prosecution, could you please answer a number of other questions? You said, General, that from the second half of 1992 the HVO used various Croatian media, the television, to spread some misinformation, slanders and abuses regarding both the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Bosniak people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since at the time you were in the hottest, if I might call it that, area, you certainly watched those programmes and read those reports?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did follow as much as I could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You certainly are familiar with the name Smiljko Sagolj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a journalist of Bosnia-Herzegovina television, if he is the one you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You know that in his propaganda programmes he often used falsified data and information, false data and information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what he used, but I know that some of his information was not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time, we ordinary citizens and I am sure you too were able to see this, were shown a document, an alleged leaflet in which the Muslims are called upon to slaughter and at the end a gross error is made in respect of Allahu Ekber -- a gross error was made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You know who Slobodan Praljak was, General?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also know who Bozo Rajic was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also know Zonko Siljak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All these people were officials in the HVO of the Croatian community of Herceg Bosna, so-called?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And their stamps figure on the documents. General, you told the Trial Chamber about the conflict in Prozor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I spoke of an aggression against Prozor, not a conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I had wanted you to repeat what you said on Thursday in answer to a question by my learned friend. You certainly know that at the time the Chief of Staff of the BiH army in Prozor was Muharem Sabic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could I now ask the technical services to show a videotape, cassette number 3, clip 1 and 2, so that the witness could identify the person in the video and that I may ask him some questions regarding it? The Prosecutor has this video. Could we ask the technical services to show clip 1 and 2, cassette number 2, Muharem Sabic. Could the text be translated as the witness has already commented on these facts? The interpreters do not have a text.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: (translating videotape). "... forty kilometres of march. My departure from the municipality of Prozor when Prozor fell after the HVO units captured the area -- after a 40 kilometre march, as I have said, and after passing the mountains and creeks, I reached free territory to inform the domestic and world public opinion of the truth as regards what happened in Prozor. "The attack by HVO units against the town of Prozor started on 23rd October 1992 about 5 pm. Before that we had a meeting of the War Presidency when we were to discuss current problems in the municipality. Until the mentioned day we had jointly dealt with combat tasks on the battle front. We fought together against the Chetniks. All areas, parts of the Prozor municipality were liberated from the Chetniks so the aggressor's boot never entered our municipality. "During the last ten days problems arose between the HVO and the TO of Prozor, or rather the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. What the causes were I do not know, but I know the consequences. As I have already said, the town itself was seized by the HVO, but not the whole municipality. Before a column of refugees old men, women and children left as their agreements were reached at the War Presidency how to overcome current problems, the stay of a Brigade and a special unit that was to pass through our municipality to go to Novi Travnik. "What its mission was, I do not know. I was told at the time that it was agreed that the main staff of the armed forces, that that unit should pass through the territory of our municipality to reach Novi Travnik. In that connection I sent a telegram to the main staff and the answer was that no such agreement was reached, that that unit was not to have passed for Novi Travnik. "This unit and group, who behaved in an unruly manner, raised tension in the town. They captured certain strategic points in the town such as the old courthouse and some other facilities and they set up new checkpoints which had not existed before. Earlier the checkpoints were held by mixed military police of the HVO and the BiH army and there were no major problems and there are records to show this, that this was just an excuse or a pretext for a general attack on Prozor. "The attack started from all weapons, artillery pieces and equipment that the HVO had in its possession. At the beginning some important strategic points in the town were captured, so as to prevent our fresh reinforcements from coming in and to prevent the evacuation of the population and the military in any direction so that we were absolutely surrounded when the attack began. When the shooting started from all possible weapons and guns, we responded and I alerted all units fully."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The second part, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: (Translating videotape). "Since I was informed that I was being looked for I took two men as an escort to try to break into free territory to inform the domestic and world public opinion as to what was happening. As I had already been informed that there were various misinformation going around, that is at 9 o'clock the Commander of the district court of Zenica, when I realised that our defences had failed and I tried to address the public through the media, and I told them what I saw with my own eyes; that is that children, women, were shot at. I heard cries of mother's children, et cetera."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have several questions in connection with this tape. Shall I begin now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: No, I think we might rise and come back at 12 o'clock. (11.27 am) (Short break) (12.00 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The witness is still on his oath, so tell him.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you, sir, that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. General, just before we broke off we watched a videotape. Do you recognise the person who spoke on that videotape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the Commander of the Territorial Defence staff in Prozor, Mr. Muharem Sabic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Sabic speak about the events that followed after the attack on Prozor in this video clip?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would first of all like to ask the Registrar to tell me, what is the number of this clip?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The video cassette is marked D89/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I would also like to tender this video clip as evidence, since the witness has recognised the person and the contents of the speech made by the person in this videotape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is submitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is submitted. General, from what we have heard from Mr. Sabic we can see that on 23rd October the HVO and parts of the Croatian army launched an attack or, as you said, aggression against Prozor, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this assault tank units led by Ante Smidt also participated, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time the assistance -- the BiH army units from Jablanica and Konjic could not provide assistance to Prozor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that that assistance never reached that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Brigade, which was located very far away in Mostar, and which had a very complicated situation in involving HVO, was not able to go there, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that at that time the TV of the Croatian community Herceg Bosna, and I am referring now to persons you already mentioned, reporters whom we already mentioned, launched reports that Muslims attacked Croats in Prozor and that Zejnil and Halilovic were behind that; are you aware of such information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did carry such reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you know that this is absolutely untrue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was in Prozor on the 26th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two or three days after those events, negotiations started in Prozor, and you also spoke about that in your interview in Jablanica, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time you were not the Commander of the 4th Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not the Commander of the 4th Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were still the Commander of the 1st Mostar Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On our side Vehbija Karic, member of the Supreme Staff Command, you and Zejnil Delalic participated in the negotiations, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I also participated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Croatian side was represented by Slobodan Praljak, Bozo Rajic, local HVO commanders and Zvonko Zovko on behalf of the Konjic HVO, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And HVO dictated the conditions of the negotiations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was in a position to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Commander Sabic said that in this video clip, but I would also like you to confirm that the -- whether you know that the majority of the Muslim population fled and was expelled and had to seek refuge in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were expelled, and I already stated that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a member of the commission you received reports about damage caused to the population of Prozor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we tried to determine what the damage was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, your Honours, I have not been able to have some documents translated, because I did not know that we would be tendering this or that the Prosecution will be tendering this, so I would just like to give some information to the witness in order to be able to ask some questions. So, I would like to have this report, which is in Bosnian, to be presented to the witness. I will not be tendering it into evidence, just as a reminder.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this makes it very difficult. We have no idea what the witness is being shown and we are just left in the dark as to what it is that the witness is being questioned about. I object to a document that has not been identified in any way being shown to a witness when we do not have any translation of it. I mean, it is very difficult for your Honours, but it makes it impossible for the Prosecution because we have no idea what it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Have you no other way of asking him questions which make him remember the contents of those documents?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I would just like him to have a look, to be reminded, and I will be asking questions or I can ask the questions even without the documents, in order not to complicate matters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: There could be a discussion between the two of you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, would you agree with me if I say that in the reports that your Prozor commission received indicated the lists of property that was taken from the citizens, the lists of buildings that were damaged or ruined, a list of buildings that had been set on fire and the destruction to other property and information that you -- the reports that you received, did they contain this kind of information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that in the reports dated January 1993, which contain an analysis of the damage, that it indicates that during the attack on Konjic 40 privately-owned businesses were destroyed, 110 vehicles stolen, and that 75 houses were burned down in Prozor -- these are houses owned by Bosniaks -- and that an additional nine houses were burnt in the hamlet of Memici; would that be approximately the information you received while you worked in the commission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You mean the attack on Prozor; you said attack on Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I composed several reports and sent them to the Supreme Command as regards Prozor. In those reports, we determined how many people were killed, wounded and expelled, how many houses were burned, looted, and the seizure of other property, such as vehicles, machinery, et cetera. I cannot remember, at this time, the exact numbers, but I think that the numbers were substantial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, the figures that you gave in your reports were substantial?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In the interview given by Commander Sabic, have you noticed that Commander Sabic said that after the attack on Prozor he advised his Superior Command -- that is the district headquarters in Zenica -- about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the municipal TO in Prozor was part of the district Territorial Defence staff in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So despite the fact that Prozor was in the area of activities of the territorial -- the Tactical Group 1, it was subordinate to the district headquarters in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The municipal headquarters in Prozor was part of the district Territorial Defence headquarters in Zenica, becoming a part of the Tactical Group 1, and the determination of the area of responsibility -- I cannot specify that. This is contained in certain documents. This Tactical Group had several directions of activity towards Prozor, towards Igman and towards Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. General, I would like to go back to the document that was shown to you by the Prosecutor on Thursday. Is it true that all our commanders in their documents referred to the "army of Bosnian Herzegovina", the "HVO", and not to "Muslim forces", "Croatian forces", is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We never used the term "Muslim forces". There was the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which later became the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and, according to the Defence Act, there was also the HVO, Croatian Defence Council, which was the recognised element of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document that was shown to you by the Prosecutor is dated 28th August, 1992. That means two months before the attack on Prozor, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the introductory part it uses terms which were never used by the -- by our forces; that is, "the Croatian/Muslim conflict", that term is used. Is that what it says there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not have the document with me, but it is probably what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I ask that document to be brought before the witness. That is the Prosecution Exhibit 189. Bearing in mind the terms used by the propaganda of the Croatian Community of Herceg Bosna, and also in view of what the text of this order looks like, is it your opinion, General, that most probably this document is a forgery?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I object to that, your Honour. I mean, if the witness is in a position to authenticate the document which he has never been put into that position, he is not in a position to say whether or not it represents a forgery. I do not see that this witness has in any way been qualified to determine whether or not he can express an opinion of whether or not it represents a forgery or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is not a proper question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Perhaps you can ask whether the document uses terms which were never used by the Bosnian army or the TO Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Suppose you ask your question on that line.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have put that question to the witness and he answered that the BiH army never used the term "Croatian/Muslim forces" in incidents by the Territorial Defence and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Just one more question so there are no misunderstandings: from the contents of this document which was allegedly dated two months before the conflict, or before the attack launched by the HVO, it is completely illogical, is it not, so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would have to analyse this document and compare it to the situation in the field at that time in order to be able to speak about its -- whether it is logical or not. As an officer of the army of Bosnian Herzegovina or the army for the federation, this document is not logical.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will not dwell on this document any longer. Your Honours, I once again find myself in a situation, since we have been supplied by the Prosecutor with a certain number of documents originating from the Croatian Community of Herceg Bosna, and they also asked several questions relating to that area, I have been unable to translate these documents supplied to us by the Prosecutor, nor have we received a translation. So I will have to adjust my questions to the decision you have reached a couple of minutes ago when I wanted to introduce a document without a translation. So you will have to excuse me if I am not completely precise. General, the documents of the Croatian Defence Council and the Croatian Community of Herceg Bosna in the heading have the Croatian chequer-board symbol at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a number of documents, some of them had a letter-head that contained the chequer-board, some of them did not. I do not know what document you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Konjic military police as early as in October 1992, and probably even before that, adopted a chequer-board as its symbol. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that they did not use the symbols, the emblems of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean the Konjic military police?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Croatian Defence Council of the Croatian Community of Herceg Bosna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A couple of minutes ago, since I am not allowed to say things, you present to me a document originating from the Croatian Community of Herceg Bosna which I , as an officer of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, do not recognise. It is a self-styled entity. I do not know of any examples that HVO units had emblems or stamps of using the emblems of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. That would be the fleur-de-lis. They only use the chequer-board.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I will now read a passage from a document from the Herceg Stjepan brigade. I would like you to answer whether such decisions and orders of the HVO did appear another that time. 15th October, 1992; this was a memo sent to the Konjic military police, saying that: "We advise you that on 17th October 1992 all people in the territory of Konjic and Jablanica who have approval for movement in the territory of Herceg Bosna and the Republic of Croatia must have that certificate certified with the stamp of the Brigade. Persons who have the approval certified with some other stamp shall be considered invalid." Do you know that HVO issued such orders, and prevented our people from moving -- restricted the freedom of movement of our people in the so-called Herceg Bosna? I share your view of its legitimacy.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I encountered such instances, even in the 1st Mostar Brigade area responsibility, and it is true that we were unable to leave the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina and to go over to the neighbouring state of Croatia unless we had the approval from the Croatian Defence Council to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. General, from your experience, you testified before this court that the freedom of movement for our convoys was restricted, that they were obstructed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there such orders in the field, orders of the HVO? I will read the contents, this one is dated 10th October 1992. It says: "Notification from the Konjic military police that a convoy, a Red Cross convoy, from Konjic was moving from Split to Konjic. It contained eight to ten trucks. It is suspected that arms for the BiH Territorial Defence are in the trucks. Please intercept the convoy. The convoy is due to reach Konjic tonight or the next day. Please report." This is signed by the commander of military police, Zeljko Brekalo. My question to you is: from your experience, are you aware that there were such or similar orders issued by the HVO for the interception of convoys?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you said that at the time for which you have information in Konjic, that is from November on, that you had information about events that we discussed. But are you aware that without the approval of the HVO it was impossible to travel from Konjic through the territory controlled by the HVO, also in the initial part of the conflict, I mean the initial period of the war in Bosnian Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly through the territory controlled by the HVO it was impossible to travel without the laissez passé, or the approval of the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like the witness to be shown an authorisation that is in possession of the Prosecutor that is dated 2nd May 1992 so that the witness can have a look at it so I can ask some questions. I have a sufficient number of copies both for the Trial Chamber and for the Prosecution, both in Bosnian and in English.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit 91/1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have looked at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it the -- a permission of the HVO, dated 2nd May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, signed by the staff Commander of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The signature, does it indicate the Commander of the municipal staff, Dinko Zebic, but signed on his behalf by Ivan Azinovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it a permission allowing Mr. Zejnil Delalic to travel through the territory under the control of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It does not indicate what area. It is an authorisation to take over the resources and when it is coming and when it is going, the convoy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By its content, is it a similar authorisation that all of you had to have to cross territory under the control of the Croatian Defence Council, the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The authorisations did not have a uniform format. They were made arbitrarily, and this is one example.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the exhibit be returned to the Registry, please? General, I should now like to ask you some questions about a different topic. You can surely confirm for the court that the road M17, that is the road going from Sarajevo to Konjic, is of strategic military importance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was of operational strategic importance for the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, General, that you are aware that there was a plan for strong JNA forces to make a break through at the beginning of May 1992, forces that were stationed in Hadzici via Prozor and Bradina to link up with the Herzegovina Corps at Borci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we had a report that there were such plans to link up those forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had that happened, General, would Sarajevo have been surrounded by a wall of more than 60 kilometres and Konjic have been entirely surrounded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot forecast what could have happened, but the situation in Sarajevo would have been a difficult one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I know that you spent much of the war period, that is the whole of 1992 and 1993, engaged in the area of Herzegovina and that you are very well aware of the conditions there. That is why I am asking you whether, as early as 1991, Herceg Bosna was first proclaimed as a cultural community of the Croatian people and shortly after that it developed as a state entity, under the name of the Croatian Community of Herceg Bosna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should like to ask the witness to be shown the Sluzbeni List, the official gazette of Herceg Bosna, of which I have one copy here in English and Bosnian. The English can be shown to the Prosecutor, which he has anyway. It was disclosed in the Blaskic case. If it could be identified and shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit 92/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, is that a document which you recognise as being headed by the words, Sluzbeni List of the Croatian Community of Herceg Bosna"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that all decisions regarding the structure of the Croatian Community of Herceg Bosna as a state entity contained in that official gazette were proclaimed by the constitutional court of Bosnia-Herzegovina as being unconstitutional.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But has not Dr. Calic spoken about it? So why repeat that? I think Dr. Calic has covered that field.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. Dr. Calic did refer to these matters. It did not submit the whole document, but the witness has certain knowledge about events which were the product of these and similar documents of Herceg Bosna. May I proceed? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I do not know if you really want to proceed because you are taking up questions which you need not. You need not bother this witness because I do not see the effect. Even if he said it was, it would not make any difference to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am not going to ask this witness about legal documents, but he knows from his own personal experience the consequences of these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: That is what your question amounts to, so it does not really matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, are you aware that in Graz, Austria, Mate Boban and Radovan Karadzic met in June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was informed about that by the media, but I am not familiar with the details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that period, disagreements and later conflicts with the HVO were intensified, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are talking about "conflicts" again. I said that it was aggression against the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina by the extremist wing of the HVO and the Croatian army. I cannot talk about a conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I am not in a position to agree or disagree with you. You have testified before this Trial Chamber about the beginnings of the misunderstandings and conflicts, which were then followed by an outspoken aggression; at least, that is my understanding of your description of your mutual relationships?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I spoke about questions which were not agreed upon between us and on the basis of those uncoordinated points, certain disagreements arose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And later on this led up to their open aggression?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to that concept of the Croatian Community of Herceg Bosna, the town of Konjic as well as the town of Mostar belonged to that para-state, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They should have belonged to the so-called Croatian Community of Herceg Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know, General, that in Konjic, before the war, the majority population -- that is more than 50 per cent of the population -- were Bosniaks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, according to the 1992 census.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that other ethnicities lived there in agreement and harmony until the aggression on Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And our country before the war, nor during the war, never considered Bosnia-Herzegovina not to be a common state of all nationalities inhabiting it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, those who attacked Bosnia on the Serbian side also felt that the Neretva River valley should belong to them and that they could separate it from this state, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was told that an agreement had been reached on the division of the Neretva River valley between a Serbian section and a Croatian section, that it would be controlled by Herceg Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also know, General, personally, that the town of Konjic was at that time exposed to heavy and continuous shelling from Serb-held positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are also aware that at the beginning of 1992, and at the beginning of the aggression on Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Croatian Defence Council was far better organised, structured and equipped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This fact, coupled with the fact that the troops may have received some kind of salary, explained why a section of the Muslim population took an active part in units of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The reasons for the participation of each individual in the HVO is the business of that individual. But it is a fact that in some units within my area of responsibility more than 60 per cent were Bosniaks in the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that after the first liberation of Mostar the Croatian Defence Council in Mostar did not take an active part in the fighting against the Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, somewhere after June 17th in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that at that same time the Konjic HVO refused to participate in the battles for the liberation of other parts of the municipality, and in the battle for lifting the blockade of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the blockade of the route M17, is it true that the area from Tarcin to Konjic, which under normal circumstances can be covered in half an hour, that it took more than 15 hours to cover this same distance by a roundabout Macadem route through Kresevo, Fojnica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, 12 to 15 hours. I covered that route.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you also spoke about the situation in the armed forces of our country at the time of the aggression. Is it true that in April our state, confronted with the aggression, quickly passed regulations to ensure the defence of the country?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
